title: Don Young Alaska Native Health Care Land Transfers Act of 2022
official_summary:
Don Young Alaska Native Health Care Land Transfers Act of 2022

This act directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to convey specified property in Alaska to certain nonprofit entities that support Alaska Native communities.

Specifically, HHS must convey specified property in (1) Tanana, Alaska, to the Tanana Tribal Council for use in connection with health and social services programs; (2) Sitka, Alaska, to the Southeast Alaska Regional Health Consortium for use in connection with health and social services programs; and (3) Anchorage, Alaska, to the Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium for use in connection with health programs.

These conveyances shall not require any consideration from, or impose any obligation, term, or condition on, the consortia or council or allow for any U.S. reversionary interest in the property.

The consortia or council shall not be liable for any environmental contamination that occurred before these conveyances.

summary.headline: This law directs the federal health department to transfer three pieces of federal property in Alaska to Alaska Native health and tribal nonprofit groups at no cost.
summary.what_it_does: The Department of Health and Human Services must give specified property in Tanana, Sitka, and Anchorage, Alaska, to named Alaska Native organizations. The transfers do not require payment or come with conditions, and the federal government cannot take the property back later. The receiving groups are not responsible for environmental contamination that happened before the transfer.

who_it_affects.how: It receives federal property in Tanana, Alaska, to use for health and social services programs, with no payment and no conditions attached.
It receives federal property in Sitka, Alaska, to use for health and social services programs, with no payment and no conditions attached.
It receives federal property in Anchorage, Alaska, to use for health programs, with no payment and no conditions attached.

who_it_affects.group: Alaska Native communities served by these organizations
who_it_affects.how: They may see health and social services offered on the transferred properties, though the law itself does not set specific service changes.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 27, 2022, and the summary does not list a separate effective date or deadline for the transfers.
